content.doc_md:
Python has two primitive loop commands:

With thewhileloop we can execute a set of statements as long as a condition is true.

Thewhileloop requires relevant variables to be ready, in this example we need to define an indexing variable,i, 
which we set to 1.

With thebreakstatement we can stop the loop even if the 
while condition is true:

With thecontinuestatement we can stop the 
current iteration, and continue with the next:

With theelsestatement we can run a block of code once when the 
condition no longer is true:

### Code Snippets

```
i = 1
while i < 6:
print(i)
i += 1

---

i = 1
while i < 6:
print(i)
if i == 3:
break
i += 1

---

i = 0
while i < 6:
i += 1
if i == 3:
continue
print(i)

---

i = 1
while i < 6:
print(i)
i += 1
else:
print("i is no longer less than 6")
```
